title: Pointed gourd (Parval): modeled ₹803/qtl left, Vansda → Surat
summary: May 2024: reported pointed gourd (Parval) prices at Vansda and Surat imply a positive modeled margin after costs on 96% of 27 matched days; a morning-report back-test averages ₹803 per quintal. No actual trade verified.
why_selected: Selected from 20 same-variety market pairs screened for pointed gourd (Parval) in May 2024; best tested candidate among the bounded set of routed finalists, not a global optimum.

evidence.observations: daily modal prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) at both markets; sale matched to the first Surat report 1–3 days after purchase
caveats: Back-test on reported prices: no actual shipment, buyer or seller is claimed.
Modal prices are reported daily aggregates, not offers anyone could be sure to get.
This data has no arrival volumes, so it cannot show whether the destination could absorb more supply; no capital-constrained or volume allocation optimum is claimed.

Costs extrapolate onion survey values (including to other crops) plus stated allowances, not freight quotes; OSRM car routing, not a verified truck route. Representative town points may not be at mandi gates.
Historical: this says what paid then, not what pays today.

scenes.headline: May 2024
scenes.caption: Vansda (Gujarat) and Surat (Gujarat) both reported pointed gourd (Parval) prices for the same variety and grade (FAQ) on 27 matched days.

scenes.headline: Two markets, two prices
scenes.caption: Vansda reported a median ₹2,750 per quintal. Surat reported a median ₹3,700 around modeled arrival days. These are not offers.

scenes.headline: Gap ₹1,150/qtl
scenes.caption: The median gap was ₹1,150 per quintal, and Surat was dearer on 100% of days.

scenes.headline: 92 km by road
scenes.caption: 92 km on OpenStreetMap roads (~1 hours by car). A loaded truck is slower, so we allow 1 days plus 7 days to get paid.

scenes.headline: After modeled costs
scenes.caption: Freight ≈₹20/qtl, 5% fees and commission, loading, 5% loss and interest. On the typical day ₹854 per quintal was left.

scenes.headline: Still positive under stress
scenes.caption: With 25% dearer freight, 10% loss and costlier credit, the typical day still kept ₹663 per quintal.

scenes.headline: A trader who only knew the morning's news
scenes.caption: Using only the latest available Surat report, the rule selects 27 of 27 modeled shipping days. 26 had positive modeled net, averaging ₹803 per quintal (₹621 under stress).

scenes.headline: The back-test
scenes.caption: The modeled Pointed gourd (Parval) route from Vansda to Surat was positive on 96% of matched days in May 2024. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹80,300, or ₹62,100 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

assumptions.value: onion survey freight applied per quintal to pointed gourd (Parval)
scaled by road km against the 1,115 km Lasalgaon→Azadpur route → ₹20/qtl here
12% a year (14% adverse) for transit + 7 days
~450 road km a day → 1 days here

conclusion: The modeled Pointed gourd (Parval) route from Vansda to Surat was positive on 96% of matched days in May 2024. At that average, a 100-quintal (10-tonne) load implies ₹80,300, or ₹62,100 under stress. Actual buyer, capacity, haggling, rejection and delays are unknown.

sources.title: Agmarknet / data.gov.in daily mandi modal prices (retained AGRINET snapshot)
RBI Working Paper WPS (DEPR) 08/2024 — Price Dynamics of Tomato, Onion and Potato
